findings.title: HYBRID_FLOOR 0.01 is applied to decay-multiplied RRF scores, mathematically excluding most of the memory corpus from proactive injection

evidence.quote:
const TEXT_ONLY_FLOOR = 0.05;  // FTS ts_rank scores: 0.05-0.5 typical
const HYBRID_FLOOR = 0.01;     // RRF fused scores: 0.01-0.03 typical

# Keep the legacy "similarity" key in sync so existing consumers
        # that read result["similarity"] see the decay-adjusted score.
        r["similarity"] = base * weight
DEFAULT_DECAY_LAMBDA = 0.02

COALESCE(1.0 / (${rrf_k_param} + f.fts_rank), 0) +
                COALESCE(1.0 / (${rrf_k_param} + v.vec_rank), 0) as rrf_score,

findings.observe_how: Math is fixed by the constants: with rrf_k=60 the max single-arm RRF score is 1/61=0.0164 and max dual-arm rank-1 is 2/61=0.0328. The JSON `score` the hook floors is similarity=base*decay (decay=exp(-age_days*0.02)). Solving 0.0164*exp(-0.02a)>=0.01 gives a<=24.7 days; 0.0328*exp(-0.02a)>=0.01 gives a<=59.4 days. So ANY single-arm match older than ~25 days and ANY match at all older than ~59 days is silently dropped, regardless of relevance. The floor comment assumes pre-decay RRF scores; the value floored is post-decay.
findings.telemetry: table-memory-recall.json: top_score p75=0.0149 (just under single-arm 0.0164 max), p50=0, hit-rate 27.4% — consistent with a corpus mostly older than the 25/59-day cutoffs.

findings.observe_how: The text-only path (search_learnings_text_only_postgres) tokenizes the query and OR-joins it before to_tsquery; the hybrid path passes the raw multi-word intent (the whole user prompt minus meta-prefixes, per extractIntent) straight into plainto_tsquery, which ANDs all lexemes. A sentence-length intent almost never matches every lexeme in any stored learning, so fts_ranked is empty and rrf_score caps at 1/(60+rank) ≈ 0.0164. Run any sentence query with --json and check fts_rank is null on all results.
findings.telemetry: top_score p75=0.0149 < dual-arm minimum (rank-1+rank-20 ≈ 0.029) across 281 logged recalls — no evidence of any dual-arm fusion ever occurring.

findings.title: Intent extraction has no guard against machine-generated prompt content: extractIntent only strips leading meta-phrases, so <task-notification> XML blobs flow through as recall queries (24.6% pollution)

evidence.quote:
const META_PATTERNS: RegExp[] = [
  /^(can you|could you|would you|please|help me|i want to|i need to|let's|lets)\s+/gi,
  /^(show me|tell me|find|search for|look for|recall|remember)\s+/gi,
const intent = gitExpanded || extractIntent(input.prompt);

findings.observe_how: New root-cause evidence for SEED-13: the only content gates before recall are prompt.length<15 and startsWith('/'). A <task-notification> or other injected XML block passes both, META_PATTERNS match nothing (anchored at ^/$ with natural-language phrases), so the full XML becomes the --query. Because the vector arm ranks the whole corpus with no absolute-similarity cutoff (D3b-08), even garbage queries return k*2 'nearest' rows that can pass the floor and inject irrelevant memories.

findings.observe_how: The 2026-05 fix widened the Python re-ping to 1.5s, but the structural TOCTOU remains: TS isDaemonReady can pass, then Python's daemon_is_alive/ping/embed (5s cap) can fail under load, routing to _embed_query_inproc whose cold sentence-transformers load (~30-45s per embedding_daemon.py docstring) is guaranteed to exceed the 12s spawnSync budget. The hook then records db_subprocess_timed_out=true and source='empty'. A budget-aware fallback (fail the embed and run FTS-only inside the same process, or an env kill-switch for in-proc embed when invoked from the hook) would convert these 12s/empty outcomes into ~1s text hits.

findings.title: Hybrid relevance gating is mathematically dead: effective threshold 0.002 is below the minimum possible top-pool RRF score (~0.0152), and the vector arm has no absolute-similarity cutoff — any query always yields k*2 'nearest' candidates

evidence.quote: similarity_threshold=args.threshold * 0.01,  # RRF scores are ~0.01-0.03 range

default=0.2,
        help="Minimum similarity threshold (default: 0.2, filters low-quality results)",

ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY embedding <=> ${embedding_param}::vector) as vec_rank
            FROM archival_memory
            WHERE {where_clause}
            AND embedding IS NOT NULL

findings.observe_how: With rrf_k=60 and LIMIT k*2=6, the worst row in the returned pool scores at least 1/(60+6)=0.0152 whenever >=6 embedded rows exist (corpus has 100+), so the 0.2*0.01=0.002 filter can never remove anything — the help text's 'filters low-quality results' is false in the default mode. Because vec_rank is pure ROW_NUMBER over cosine distance with no cutoff, a nonsense query ranks the corpus identically to a good one; the only differences are which rows are 'nearest'. Consequence: the memory_recall_relevance Braintrust score (topScoreRaw) measures rank arithmetic + age, not semantic relevance — it is decision-risky to tune floors against it.
findings.telemetry: top_score p25/p50=0, p75=0.0149 — the distribution is bimodal empty-vs-0.015, exactly what rank-only scoring predicts.

notes: Core thesis: the 27.4% hit-rate is a pipeline-math problem, not a corpus problem. The hook floors a decay-multiplied score (HYBRID_FLOOR=0.01 vs max achievable single-arm RRF 0.0164 * exp(-age*0.02)), and the hybrid FTS arm never fuses because plainto_tsquery ANDs the whole prompt — so the achievable score band is exactly the 0-0.0164 band telemetry shows (p75=0.0149). Three independent quick wins would move the number: (a) floor the pre-decay base_score (already emitted in JSON) or lower HYBRID_FLOOR below 0.0164*expected-decay; (b) OR-tokenize the hybrid FTS query like the text-only path already does; (c) fix or delete the 2000ms local arm. Latency: the 13-17s is double uv cold-start plus serialization plus a doomed in-proc embed fallback; daemon infrastructure itself is sound.
